title: Probe item
description: One benchmark item. Stratification fields are required because the whole design rests on comparing behaviour ACROSS strata - a pooled number would hide the effect we most expect to find.

id.description: Stable identifier. Results reference this, so it must never be reused for different content.

answerable.description: Ground truth for abstention scoring: SHOULD the model answer at all?

category.description: AbstentionBench taxonomy, plus three of ours: 'coherent-false-premise' (retained as a stratum; the mechanism claim was cut 2026-08-17), 'counterfactual' (KUQ's counterfactual questions — 'what if X had not happened' — which have no factual answer), and 'missing-context' (the answer is not in the passage the item supplies; SQuAD 2.0's unanswerables). See docs/METRICS.md.

domain.description: Domain-level stratification. Required because the quantisation effect on calibration is reported at domain level, so pooling would mask it.

difficulty.description: Optional but valuable: large models modulate confidence by difficulty and small ones reportedly do not. This field is how we test that here.

scoring.description: Must be mechanically checkable. If an item needs a judge model to score, it does not belong in the set - it introduces a confound and unbounded cost. 'set-contains' is set-match with the answer containing a gold on token boundaries (answer ⊇ gold, one direction — 'Jani' must not match 'Jani Beg'), for extractive QA where 'The Mongol army under Jani Beg' must count against gold 'Jani Beg' — exact match would score a confident correct answer as an error, the worst direction for Type-2 AUROC. It over-credits list answers that merely include the gold; stated where used.

answer.description: For method 'choice': the exact text of the correct option, NOT its index. Index-based answers silently break when options are permuted, which is precisely what validity screen #4 does.

paraphrase_of.description: If set, this item is a reworded twin of the referenced id. Used by validity screen #3 (stability under paraphrase).

options.description: Forced-choice alternatives, in canonical order. Presence of this field makes the item forced-choice. REQUIRED for a well-defined Type-1 decision: meta-d'/M-ratio are undefined without one (arXiv 2603.25112), and open-ended items also gave every model a 100% score, leaving Type-2 AUROC with no negative class. Distractors must be plausible enough that a competent model can actually fail - an item everyone aces measures nothing. maxItems 10 (was 6) to admit MMLU-Pro's ten-option items; the harness enumerates letters A..J.

context.description: The passage the question is about, if any (extractive QA). The prompt already embeds it; this copy is what the gate's grounding check reads — 'does the answer appear verbatim in the passage'. Optional.
